# Presentation Rewrite: Design Spec

**Date:** 2026-07-02
**Status:** Draft for user review
**Scope:** Complete from-scratch rewrite of `workspace/presentation/presentation-script.md` and the HTML slide deck generated by `workspace/presentation/generate.py`. Presentation-only: no `src/` changes (see Section 7).

## 1. Purpose

Turn the current 30-minute documentation-style walkthrough into a 20-minute desk pitch that convinces traders and quants to adopt the RV-forecast signal for GSVIVS01. The old script read tables aloud, explained the variance-swap strike after the section that depended on it, duplicated two "Part 6" headings, and buried its best material (Sharpe story, h=22 humility result) at minute 25. The rewrite is results-first: state the claim by minute 5, then earn it.

## 2. Locked requirements

| Requirement | Decision |
|---|---|
| Occasion | Desk pitch for adoption |
| Audience | Traders + quants mixed; light on textbook material |
| Length | ~20 min talk + open Q&A |
| Dashboard | Frequent toggles; the dashboard is the primary evidence surface |
| Deck | Full rewrite inside `generate.py`; keep `./vol present` CLI contract |
| Visual design | Dark terminal palette, serif display type, amber for structure, green only for wins |
| Typography rule | No em dashes anywhere in deck or script |
| Equations | Exactly two rendered equations: variance-swap strike (Kvar) and QLIKE |
| Numbers rule | No magic numbers; every number labeled or translated; raw QLIKE levels live on the dashboard only |
| Inline deep-dives | Leakage/purged CV and SHAP+ALE only; QLIKE-vs-MSE and stat tests get one sentence each plus Q&A backstop |
| Script form | Verbatim spoken script + one-page beat sheet |
| Signal definition | Binary short/flat (stand aside); the old script's "go long the strip" wording is wrong |
| Ending | No explicit ask; recap, open floor |
| Q&A backstop | `qa-comprehensive.md` unchanged |

## 3. Content architecture

### 3.1 Talk arc (~20 min)

1. **The product and its problem** (2.5 min). GSVIVS01 mechanics in plain words; equity curve; drawdown days are the days it sold variance anyway. Ends on: "it sells variance on the days it should not."
2. **The claim** (1.5 min). 09:10 decision rule (forecast vs strike), Kvar explained in 30 seconds with the VIX-style integral, headline Sharpe 1.60 to 1.95. Dashboard moment 1.
3. **The model** (4 min). HAR-IV spine carrying most of the forecast; LightGBM residual overlay via init_score, end-to-end in QLIKE; tenor matching; feature map slide.
4. **Why trust the number** (4.5 min). Purged expanding-window walk-forward, panel-aware date splits, purged early stopping, five-seed rule. QLIKE equation with trader gloss. Dashboard moment 2 (rankings; DM and MCS as one-sentence pointers).
5. **What it learned** (4 min). Beeswarm reading guide, then live SHAP tour and one ALE curve. Dashboard moments 3 and 4.
6. **Where it wins and where it doesn't** (2.5 min). Relative QLIKE improvements at h=1/h=5; h=22 linear wins, framed as knowing when to stop; MSE one-liner (Sharpe 0.3).
7. **Close** (1 min). Three caveats, three numbers, open floor; dashboard free-roams during Q&A.

Content as validated in storyboard v3 (`.superpowers/brainstorm/701-1782946370/content/storyboard-v3.html`):

| # | Kicker | Title | Diagram (SVG) | Equation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ML Vol Forecasting | Timing the Variance Seller | faint variance-swap payoff motif | none |
| 2 | The product and its problem | GSVIVS01 sells variance every single day | trading-day timeline + 4y equity curve with red drawdown ticks labeled "realized > strike" | none |
| 3 | The claim | Every morning: compare the forecast to the strike | none (morning sequence described in script) | Kvar OTM-option integral, glossed "same integral as the VIX; it inherits the skew, so it sits above ATM IV" |
| 4 | The model | A linear spine and a tree overlay | flow: inputs -> HAR-IV spine -> residual trees -> forecast; tenor-matching inset (1d/0DTE, 5d/1w, 22d/1m) | none |
| 5 | The features | Four things the market tells you | four-quadrant map: price history / options surface / measurement quality / calendar, plain-word examples, ~128 total | none |

Slide text: full self-describing sentences as in storyboard v3, not fragments. Slide 9 stays on screen through Q&A.

### 3.3 Dashboard choreography (4 planned moments + free-roam)

| Moment | After slide | Tab | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 3 | GSVIVS | Prove the Sharpe claim on live evidence; stand-aside precision |
| D2 | 6 | Rankings | Raw QLIKE levels, OOS period, DM and MCS columns as pointers |
| D3 | 7 | SHAP beeswarm (h=1) | Top-5 features tied to trader concepts |
| D4 | after D3 | ALE (h=1, 0-DTE IV) | One curve: information content highest in the tail |

### 3.4 Content style rules

- No em dashes in any deliverable text (script, slides, beat sheet).
- Exactly two rendered equations (Kvar, QLIKE); all other math in words or diagrams.
- Every on-slide number passes one of: (a) instantly priceable by a trader (Sharpe, % of days), (b) labeled with what/period/baseline, or (c) cut. Raw QLIKE levels appear only on the dashboard.
- Relative framing for forecast-loss improvements ("about 10% lower forecast loss than the strongest linear baseline"), bps optionally in the spoken script, never bare on slides.
- Spoken register: short sentences, transitions hand off explicitly, numbers spoken with meaning attached.

## 4. Script specification

- File: `workspace/presentation/presentation-script.md`, rewritten from scratch.
- Verbatim spoken script, 2,600 to 2,800 words (20 min at a natural pace), first person, present tense.
- Cue format: `> [SLIDE n: title]` and `> [DASHBOARD: tab, what to point at]` placed at the exact sentence where they fire.
- Each of the 7 arc sections ends with a written transition sentence into the next.
- Header block keeps the regeneration instructions (`./vol present` usage) currently at the top of the script.
- After the script: a one-page beat sheet. Per slide: 3 to 5 beats, the transition line verbatim, and the one number that matters on that slide.
- The 230-line SHAP appendix and Q&A cue cards are removed from the script file; `qa-comprehensive.md` already covers them and is not modified.

## 5. Deck technical specification

- `workspace/presentation/generate.py` rewritten from scratch; same CLI: `--dashboard-path` (relative from the output HTML to the dashboard file) and `--output` (default `workspace/presentation/presentation.html`). Registered `vol present` subcommand unchanged (root `vol` line 324).
- Output: one self-contained HTML file. No CDN, no network fetches, system font stacks only (Georgia/Times serif for display, Segoe UI/Verdana sans for labels and body).
- Theme tokens (from approved V2 mockup): background #0c1117, ink #e8e4da, muted #7d8896 and #9aa5b1, hairline #1f2a37, amber #e8b339 (structure, emphasis), green #4cc38a (wins only), serif display, small-caps letterspaced amber kickers.
- Layout: fixed 16:9 stage (1280x720 design grid) scaled to the window via CSS transform; works on any projector resolution.
- JS (vanilla, minimal): arrow keys/space/PgUp-PgDn navigation, D toggles dashboard overlay, slide counter bottom-right, no other chrome.
- Dashboard toggle: full-viewport iframe overlay, lazy-loaded on first toggle; if the dashboard file is missing, show a labeled placeholder panel instead of a broken iframe (this is the local-dev situation).
- Equations: authored as LaTeX strings in `generate.py`, pre-rendered at build time to SVG via matplotlib mathtext (matplotlib 3.10.9 confirmed in the project venv), inlined into the HTML, colored to theme. No runtime math dependency.
- Mock dashboard fixture: `workspace/presentation/tournament_dashboard_mock.html`, a minimal tabbed HTML file with a clear MOCK banner, checked in for local toggle testing.

## 6. Diagram system (7 inline SVGs)

Quality standard: hand-authored inline SVG on an 8px grid; one shared stroke width; shared arrowhead marker defs; palette colors only; hatch pattern reserved exclusively for purge gaps; sans labels at consistent sizes; every axis titled with units; no decorative elements that do not encode information.

1. Slide 1: variance-swap payoff motif, faint, background only.
2. Slide 2: trading-day timeline (09:30 sell strip, delta-hedge, 16:00 MOC settle) + equity curve 100 to 138 with drawdown days ticked red and labeled.
3. Slide 4: architecture flow with tenor-matching inset.
4. Slide 5: four-quadrant feature map.
5. Slide 6: expanding-window folds with hatched purge gaps and panel-split note.
6. Slide 7: beeswarm reading guide.
7. Slide 8: per-horizon improvement bars, h=22 flipped.

Data-bearing diagrams (equity curve, result bars) hardcode their series from Section 3.5 canonical numbers with a source comment; the deck build never touches the data cache.

## 7. Dashboard dark theme: DROPPED (2026-07-02)

Investigation during planning showed the tournament dashboard is already dark (`--bg-primary: #1a1a2e`, cyan accent, dark Plotly and Mermaid themes in `src/volforecast/visualization/templates/tournament_dashboard.html`). The anti-flash rationale from the interview was based on a wrong premise. User decision: drop the workstream entirely; no `src/` changes. The navy+cyan dashboard reads as "the tool", the near-black+amber deck as "the talk".

## 8. Repo strategy (dual tree)

- The presentation tooling exists only in the tracked root snapshot (`workspace/presentation/`); the runnable working copy `ml-vol-estimator/` has no `workspace/presentation/` and its patched `vol` lacks the `present` subcommand.
- Dev loop: edit tracked root `workspace/presentation/generate.py` and run it with the working copy's venv via `ml-vol-estimator/vol shell`. Porting the `present` subcommand into the working copy's `vol` (OS-guarded, consistent with existing local patches) is optional polish, not required.
- No `src/` changes in this project (Section 7), so the regression gate and mirroring workflow are not needed.
- TDD for `generate.py` (it is Python, so the repo's TDD rule applies): tests live in `workspace/presentation/test_generate.py`, run via `ml-vol-estimator/vol shell -m pytest`.

## 9. Out of scope

- `qa-comprehensive.md` (kept as-is as the Q&A backstop).
- EDRVS Kvar caching, LSTM trial-051, any model or data work.
- Regenerating the real tournament dashboard (GS-only).
- Restyling any other visualization output.

## 10. Risks and open items

- **Numbers freshness:** all Section 3.5 values carry a [VERIFY on GS] flag; the talk must not ship with stale numbers.
- **matplotlib mathtext coverage:** mathtext handles the two equations' LaTeX subset (integrals, fractions, subscripts); if rendering quality disappoints, fallback is hand-set SVG typography for those two equations.
- **Dashboard tab names:** D1 to D4 cue names (GSVIVS, Rankings, SHAP, ALE) must be checked against the real dashboard's tab labels on GS; the mock fixture mirrors whatever the real labels are.
- **Working-copy vol lacks `present`:** acceptable (run generate.py directly); porting the subcommand is optional polish.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

- Script: 2,600 to 2,800 words of spoken text; zero em dashes (checkable by grep); cues placed at exact sentences; every number labeled per Section 3.4; reads aloud in 19 to 21 minutes.
- Beat sheet: fits one page; per slide beats + transition + key number.
- Deck: builds offline via `vol present` semantics; 9 slides; exactly two equation SVGs; 7 themed diagrams meeting Section 6 standard; keyboard nav and D-toggle work; graceful placeholder without a dashboard; no external requests (verifiable by inspecting the HTML for http references).
- No diff under `src/` (root or working copy) at project end.
